newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran president blast German court verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iran president blast German court verdict.

text.p: Some 3,000 hardline Islamists marched on the German embassy in Tehran on Friday, and some pelted the building with tomatoes to protest a German court ruling that Iran ordered political murders, witnesses said.

Iran's president said the diplomatic row over the Berlin court verdict on Thursday that top political and religious leaders in Tehran had ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents was a passing storm provoked by the U.S. and Israel.

"The (U.S. and Israel) needed such a propaganda wave. We should expect them to keep up the noise in the West. But this will bring them nothing. It is like a thunderstorm that brings clear weather in its wake," Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, a Shi'ite Moslem cleric, said in a sermon to thousands of worshippers gathered at the Tehran University campus for Friday prayers.

After the prayers, about 3,000 hardline demonstrators marched four km (2.5 miles) to the German embassy in central Tehran. Many pelted it with tomatoes and a few threw stones but stopped after police warnings, witnesses said.

The members of the Ansar-e Hizbollah (Supporters of the party of God) group chanted "This is the second den of spies" -- likening it to the United States embassy which was seized by radical Islamic students in 1979, the witnesses said.

Many carried pictures of Iran's late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini and his successor Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Protestors chanted "Death to Germany", "Fascist Germany, servant of Zionism", "Death to America" and "Death to Israel".

The demonstrators rushed a line of riot police behind barriers at the embassy but were pushed back. In a resolution, protestors demanded Germany apologise by Tuesday for what they called an affront to Iran and the Islamic world and urged Tehran to sever ties if Bonn refused.
"This (verdict) is a historic disgrace for the German judiciary and claims that Germany's legal system is independent are now totally in question," Rafsanjani said.

"Not only were they (the court) not independent from their own government, but they were even dependent on foreigners. We have no doubt that American and Israeli agents have had a finger in this," he said in the sermon carried by Tehran radio.
Rafsanjani told worshippers the row with Germany and the European Union (EU) was hurting European interests more than those of Iran.
Germany has withdrawn its ambassador from Tehran and asked four Iranian diplomatic staff to leave the embassy in Bonn. Iran also recalled its ambassador and expelled four German diplomats.

The EU on Thursday invited its members to recall their ambassadors from Tehran. Sweden, Belgium, Finland and France withdrew their ambassadors on Friday and Britain said it was recalling its charge d'affaires.
"Was it not so in the Salman Rushdie affair that all of them recalled their ambassadors and later disgracefully sent them back with apologies?" Rafsanjani said.

European Community member states recalled their ambassadors in 1989 from Iran over the death edict against the British author by the late Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini for alleged blasphemy. The EC allowed the envoys to return after a month and most went back to Tehran.
Rafsanjani said Iran was stronger economically than in 1989 and did not need the EU, and derided the EU call to recall envoys as "airs put on by a 60-year-old bride".
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi also criticised the EU's decision to cut off its "critical Iran dialogue" with Tehran over the verdict.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said the court did not follow legal procedures and "solely relied on remarks of a number of terrorists and hijackers, for whose arrest warrants have been issued by the Iranian judiciary".

Zarif was referring to the court's use of testimonies by Iranian opposition members including Abolhassan Banisadr -- Iran's first president who fled to France after being deposed in 1981. Tehran accuses Banisadr of hijacking and other crimes.
